input.prompt:
You are auditing accessibility for one step ("SFCC-795 accessibility sweep") of an in-flight Zimmermann PWA Kit cart build. Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-11_cart (already checked out, clean tree — do not switch branches or edit any repo files, you are auditing only, not building).

Two other sub-agents are covering different angles in parallel — stay in your lane: one runs the automated Storybook a11y test-runner tool, one does static code reading (grepping aria-labels/alt text, diffing a live-region block against base). Your job is exclusively LIVE BROWSER measurement via Playwright — real Tab key presses, real computed styles, real bounding-box geometry, real DOM text content. Never assume or describe a value from reading source; drive the browser and read back what actually happens.

## Environment facts (already confirmed, don't re-verify)

- Storybook dev server is live at http://localhost:6006 (HTTP 200 confirmed on `/` and `/iframe.html`).
- The `playwright` npm package (v1.60.0) is installed in the repo's node_modules, and Chromium browser binaries are ALREADY downloaded and cached at `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright` (chromium-1243 present). This means a plain Node script that does `const { chromium } = require('/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/playwright'); const browser = await chromium.launch();` will work directly — you do NOT need `npx playwright install` and you must NOT run `npx playwright test` or touch `playwright.config.*` in any way (it's a frozen/Tier 1 test-config file per this repo's rules — never modify it, never rely on it, just use the Playwright library API directly in a standalone script).
- Write any script(s) you need ONLY inside this scratch directory: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/6017b702-06fb-4295-9164-1c708495531a/scratchpad` — never create files inside the actual repo tree.
- Storybook's iframe URL pattern for a single story is `http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=<story-id>&viewMode=story`. Get real story IDs from `http://localhost:6006/index.json` (or `/stories.json` as fallback) rather than guessing the slug format.

## Two established facts about this codebase — already confirmed by direct code reading, do NOT re-derive them, build your testing plan around them

**(a) The real cart-item quantity control is NOT `ZimmQuantityStepper`.** `overrides/app/components/product-item/index.tsx` (line 277) renders `<ProductQuantityPicker>` (`overrides/app/components/product-item/product-quantity-picker.tsx`), which wraps the BASE, unstyled `QuantityPicker` from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/quantity-picker` — a Chakra `useNumberInput`-based number input with increment/decrement buttons whose accessible names are "Increment Quantity for {productName}" / "Decrement Quantity for {productName}", and `min={0}`. The separately-built `ZimmQuantityStepper` molecule (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmQuantityStepper/`) is never imported or rendered anywhere in production code — it is fully orphaned (confirmed via exhaustive grep). You must test BOTH surfaces and report them SEPARATELY, clearly labeled — do not conflate "the real stepper" with "the orphaned ZimmQuantityStepper story."

**(b) "Remove" / "Move to Wishlist" links do not exist yet anywhere in this repo.** The component that would render them (`ZimmCartItemActions`) is a later, not-yet-built plan step. The current `Commerce/ProductItem` stories that pass a `secondaryActions` prop use a placeholder plain `<button type="button">Edit</button>` in that slot instead — test this placeholder for completeness, but be explicit in your report that it is NOT "Remove"/"Move to Wishlist" and does not verify that part of the checklist.

## Task — for every item, report the REAL measured number or string, never an assumed/described one

1. **Real ProductItem walkthrough.** Load `Commerce/ProductItem`'s `WithWarningMessage` story (get its real story ID from index.json) via the iframe URL. From a fresh page load, press Tab repeatedly (cap at 15 presses) and after each press record `document.activeElement`'s tag name, role, and accessible name (aria-label or text content). Report the full observed sequence. State plainly whether non-interactive content (image, name, price, the inline message text) is correctly skipped by Tab — the checklist phrase "image → name → price → stepper → message → Remove → Wishlist" may describe visual/reading order rather than literal Tab stops; say which your data supports.
2. **Focus-visible, real computed styles — real stepper's two buttons.** For the increment/decrement buttons found in step 1: capture `getComputedStyle()` for `outline`, `outlineOffset`, `outlineColor`, `boxShadow` in the default (unfocused) state and again after Tab-focusing each. Report all raw values and state plainly whether default vs focus-visible actually differ.
3. **Target size, real geometry — same two buttons.** `getBoundingClientRect()` width/height in real px. State pass/fail against "≥24px" with the real numbers.
4. **Keyboard operability, real interaction.** Tab to the increment button, press Enter — confirm via the visible quantity `<input>`'s actual value (before/after) that it increased by 1. Repeat with Space on the decrement button, confirming decrease.
5. **Boundary/disabled behaviour, real.** Repeatedly decrement via keyboard from the story's starting quantity. Does the decrement button reach a real `disabled` state (check the actual `disabled` attribute / `aria-disabled`, and confirm further Enter/Space has no effect)? At what quantity value? Report the real observed floor, and flag explicitly if it reaches 0 rather than 1 (the orphaned ZimmQuantityStepper's own spec calls for disabling at quantity 1 — if the real component's floor differs, name that gap).
6. **Live-region real-time correctness.** Find the `role="status"` element in the DOM (a visually-hidden element rendered by ProductQuantityPicker). Capture its `textContent` immediately before an increment click and immediately after. Report both strings verbatim and state plainly whether the announced quantity actually updated to match the new visible input value, or stayed stale.
7. **The orphaned `ZimmQuantityStepper`, separately.** Read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmQuantityStepper/index.stories.tsx` for its real title/export names, load its story, and repeat measurements 2-5 above against THIS component's own two buttons — clearly labeled as testing the orphaned/unwired component.
8. **The placeholder "Edit" secondaryActions button.** In the WithWarningMessage (or similar) ProductItem story, find the "Edit" button and repeat the focus-visible (step 2) and target-size (step 3) measurements on it — clearly labeled "placeholder stub, not the real Remove/Wishlist links."
9. **ZimmCartDrawer close button.** Read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/index.stories.tsx` for its title/exports, load a story, locate the close button (find it by role=button, report its real accessible name), and repeat the focus-visible and target-size measurements on it.
10. **No colour-only reliance — empirical check on the real stepper's disabled state.** When the decrement (or increment) button is disabled per step 5, check whether it ALSO carries a real `disabled` HTML attribute or `aria-disabled="true"` (read `outerHTML` or the relevant attribute directly) — not just a visual/colour change.

## Report back

For every measurement: the real number/string you observed, and a one-line pass/fail against the stated requirement. If a story or element genuinely can't be found, say so and describe what you tried — never fabricate a result. Do not edit or fix any project file.
